And empathy is more than just putting yourself in someone else's shoes... it's about being in their state of mind. Let's look at a couple of examples:

Let's say your friend's grandfather dies. Your friend is obviously sad. If you have never lost a grandparent or family member, you can only be sympathetic. But, if you HAVE lost a grandparent or family member, then you can be empathetic, as you know how they feel, and can share their feelings.

If your brother is about to fail a class, and he's scared that he won't be able to pass... if you're never been in that situation, you can choose to be sympathetic or not, and feel bad for him or not... if you've failed a class, like that, then you can "put yourself in his shoes" and feel how he feels.

Do you believe this inability to feel empathy influences your politics?

On the contrary, I believe that my lack of empathy gives me the ability to see politics for what they are... it's everyone else who's empathy is influencing THEIR politics. I consider myself one of the few who can wade through the political cesspool, unhindered. I know that doesn't make sense, so let's take a look at an example: the recent mass shooting in Florida.

Many people are going to react emotionally to this, in one way or another. Either they're going to be mad at Muslims/ISIS, or they're going to be mad at "assault rifles" and gun laws. This anger will, undoubtedly, sway MANY votes towards either Hilary or Trump, respectively, due to their stances.

For me, I couldn't care less. I didn't know any of the people killed... I didn't know the shooter... I've only been to Orlando once in my life... I have no dog in this fight. My life on Saturday was, in no way, different than my life on Sunday or Monday (with the exception of seeing non-stop Voat posts about Orlando).

My vote isn't going to be swayed by something as fickle as an emotion, or the shooting in FL. I know that NEITHER candidate can do ANYTHING to curb the next mass shooting, and my lack of anger (contributed to my lack of empathy) allows me to see this clearly. And, since I see this, my vote is unchanged by this "tragic" event which I care so little about.

Everyone else, on the other hand, cannot see through their seething anger/depression, and is therefore attacking/defending either a religion or weapons... as if this will bring back those people, or stop the next shooting, or change anything at all.

Do you ever consider if there would be any objective value in feeling empathy?

No.

As I outlined above, I've found that empathy "gets in the way" with successfully going about my day. I won't "fake" feeling bad for anyone for any reason... it doesn't do me any good. To me, any value empathy provides can be trumped ten times over by NOT having empathy. In other words: you give me one story where having empathy is beneficial, and I'll not only tell you why it wasn't genuinely valuable to your story, but give you ten stories to show you why, and ten more where empathy was a hindrance.

Does a lack of empathy negatively impact your life in other ways?

I find that I don't "relate" to people very well. Some would call this a negative, but I again... don't care. Please, let me explain:

Of the friends I have, I believe they will be friends for life... but making new friends tends to be difficult. Most people perceive me as simply being an asshole, and I'm just fine with that. If they don't want to take the time to actually learn who I am, why I am the way I am, or what I think about certain topics, before they make a judgment call on what kind of person I am, I don't want to waste the time feigning for their attention... because that's what it is: a waste of my time.

Again, some would see that having only a few friends is a negative, but I see it as a positive. They're willing to stop and listen before making a judgment call, and I'd rather have that kind of friend than one that will judge right off the bat.

Perhaps something like being unable to understand why people do certain things or being able to predict how people will react or handle certain things because of an inability to empathize?

Most people can predict their actions up to, and only until, they reach an emotional decision-making point.

They know that they'll buy a pet, love their pet, take good care of it, and feed it every day... but they can't say exactly what they'd do when a hard decision comes up.

When will they have to put it down, and why? Will it be of old age? Will the pet get maimed by a car? Will it get cancer... and THEN will they pay for the cancer or just have the pet put down?!?!

The reason this obscurity arises is because of emotion. They're scared, excited, or sad about what will happen when they put their pet down, and they don't even want to think about it... so they don't know what will happen when that time comes... but I know what they'll end up doing...

The cancer treatments are too expensive, even for a human. That dog's old, sick, and dying... put it down. Even if the pet survives being hit by a car, it'll never again be the same... put it down. Your pet is almost 20, it's not getting any younger... put it down.
